newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil motorcycle sales seen up sharply this year.
newsitem.headline: Brazil motorcycle sales seen up sharply this year.

text.p: SAO PAULO, June 17 (reuter) - Brazil's motorcycle industry may sell 380,000 units this year, some 100,000 or 36 percent more nationally produced bikes than were sold last year, Gazeta Mercantil newspaper said.
"Sales have never been so good," the paper quoted Abraciclo industry association chief Franklim Mello Neto as saying.
The paper said Brazil's motorcycle manufacturers are producing at near-capacity and sales outlets are reporting low or no stocks.
In response to the strong demand, Brazilian market leader Honda plans to expand production at its Manaus plant and build a new unit in Brazil's central state of Goias, it said.
Honda holds an 89.4-percent local market share and imports account for just five percent of the bikes sold in Brazil, the paper said.
